gloss: extremely; excessively; to an extreme degree

definitions.gloss: extremely; excessively; to an extreme degree
definitions.explanation: Indicates that something is at a level far beyond what is normal, reasonable, or expected. Often carries a negative nuance, suggesting that the degree is unbalanced or unhealthy, though it can also be used neutrally to emphasize extreme values or behavior.

examples.japanese: {極端|きょくたん}に{少|すく}ない。
{彼女|かのじょ}は{極端|きょくたん}に{恥|は}ずかしがりだ。
{極端|きょくたん}にダイエットすると{体|からだ}を{壊|こわ}す。
examples.english: If you diet to an extreme, you will ruin your health.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}、{物価|ぶっか}が{極端|きょくたん}に{上|あ}がっているように{感|かん}じる。
examples.english: Lately, it feels like prices have been rising to an extreme degree.

notes:
The adverbial form of the na-adjective {極端|きょくたん} (extreme), formed by adding に. Describes an action, state, or change that goes well beyond normal limits.

USAGE:
- Often implies imbalance or undesirability — something has swung too far in one direction.
- Commonly modifies verbs describing change ({減|へ}る, {増|ふ}える, {変|か}わる) and adjectives describing quantity or quality ({少|すく}ない, {多|おお}い, {高|たか}い, {低|ひく}い).
- Can be softened with {少|すこ}し to {少|すこ}し{極端|きょくたん}に ("a bit extremely"), though {極端|きょくたん}すぎる (too extreme) is more natural for criticism.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {極端|きょくたん}に{少|すく}ない: extremely few
- {極端|きょくたん}に{走|はし}る: to go to extremes
- {極端|きょくたん}に{変|か}わる: to change drastically
- {極端|きょくたん}に{嫌|きら}う: to hate intensely
- {極端|きょくたん}な{例|れい}: an extreme example

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {非常|ひじょう}に: extremely — neutral, broadly applicable, no implication of imbalance
- とても: very — everyday speech, weaker than {極端|きょくたん}に
- ものすごく: tremendously — colloquial, emphasizes large degree without the "off-balance" nuance
- やたらと: excessively / indiscriminately — similar negative nuance but suggests lack of reason or restraint
